A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ELU-GCN despite the changed title and format. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification experiments on eleven datasets, component ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary analyses (Tables 1–2; Appendix G).

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments on eleven datasets and reports revised results and additional fusion-weight sensitivity results (Tables 1–2; Appendix F).

M1.justification: v2 replaces the feature-uniformity penalty in v1 Eq. (10) with prediction entropy in Eq. (12), and changes output fusion from averaging softmax probabilities to applying softmax after averaging logits. The specified graph update also changes from H Q^T to Q H^T, propagated through the iterative formulas. These materially revise the computation and objective within the retained two-stage framework.

E1.justification: Both evaluate node classification on the same eleven citation, co-purchase, webpage and social-network datasets. The added hyperparameter sweep introduces no new dataset, population or task scenario.

E2.justification: The corresponding main benchmark, social-network and runtime comparisons retain their respective twelve, five and two baselines. Added related-work citations do not introduce evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Benchmark splits, sample counts and classification metrics remain unchanged. v2 adds a fusion-weight η sweep on Cora and Citeseer and removes the training-versus-validation-loss evaluation. Appendix F.2 states an η range of 0.1–1.0, although Figure 6 plots 0.0–0.9.

E4.justification: The generalization-gap analysis in v1 Section 3.2.4 and Figure 4 is removed, not relocated. v2 adds η sensitivity analysis and revises the λ/τ analysis in Appendix F.2. Component ablations, graph visualizations and NELU-node analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same ± reporting practice in result tables. Neither specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, explains the uncertainty estimates, or adds confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise six full-model means, including Cora 84.04→84.29, Citeseer 73.17→74.23 and Squirrel 60.91→56.91; Pubmed remains 80.51. Baseline and social-network scores are unchanged. Runtime–accuracy points and sensitivity findings also change, η results are added, and generalization-gap results are removed. These are revised-method results, with mixed changes rather than uniform gains.

T1.justification: The gradient, closed-form solution and associated Woodbury expressions are revised to use Q H^T, correcting the earlier factor ordering. The label-influence and generalization statements and proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged. The revised auxiliary P expression in v2 Appendix A.2 introduces a dimensional inconsistency by placing H H^T before a c-by-c inverse.

C1.justification: v2's introduction newly claims parameter-free ELU-graph construction. The principal contributions concerning effective label utilization, graph construction, contrastive learning, generalization and empirical superiority otherwise retain their earlier scope.

C2.justification: The regularizer's explanation changes from preventing representation collapse to encouraging decision boundaries in low-density regions (v1 Section 2.3; v2 Section 3.3). The interpretation of measured generalization gaps as confirmation of the theory disappears with that analysis; the main graph-complementarity interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-release URL but removes v1 Appendix D.2's explicit two-layer GCN formulas, ReLU specification, shared weights and graph choice at each layer. It also omits the S(0)=I statement. These are documentation changes; omission does not establish that the underlying architecture was abandoned.

R1.justification: The advanced-GCN discussion is refocused on GCN/LPA combinations, including PTA, GPL, UniMP and GCN-LPA. v2 adds MixMatch and a different Wu et al. (2024) work, removes several earlier citations, and explicitly credits Wang and Leskovec (2021) for the proof idea in Appendix B.1.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: it retitles the paper, introduces main-text Related Works while retaining Appendix C, reorganizes experimental subsections, integrates runtime analysis into Experiments, and removes duplicate pseudocode/runtime appendices. It also brings an existing appendix derivation into the main text and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout with full-width displays. Figure 2's panels are restacked, sensitivity surfaces are redrawn, an η plot is added, and the generalization-gap plot and duplicate runtime display are removed. Figures, tables and captions are extensively repositioned or reformatted.

improvement.justification: The corrected graph solver, more focused prior-work discussion, added η analysis and code-release pointer provide benefits. However, v2 removes explicit branch-architecture details and empirical generalization-gap evidence while retaining the generalization claims, and introduces a dimensional inconsistency in Appendix A.2. These gains and losses leave the net quality direction unclear; the mixed accuracy changes do not resolve that tradeoff.
